goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — An enabled feed returning HTTP 404 aborts retrieval before fetch_http, leaving every new embed loading indefinitely even when its article is reachable.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 35-47, the perform_retrieve method first checks if TopicEmbed already exists, then if feed_polling_enabled? it calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}), and then checks again if TopicEmbed exists. If the embed still doesn't exist after polling, it calls fetch_http. The finding claims that if the RSS feed returns HTTP 404, it 'aborts retrieval before fetch_http'. However, examining the code flow: if PollFeed fails (e.g., 404), it would raise an exception in SimpleRSS.parse or open(), but this would propagate up and not prevent fetch_http from being called - the exception would abort the entire perform_retrieve method. But more importantly, looking at the actual code structure, there's no explicit error handling that would cause a 404 to specifically skip fetch_http while continuing execution. If the RSS poll fails with an exception, the whole method fails. If it succeeds but doesn't find the URL, fetch_http is called. The finding's specific claim about 'aborts retrieval before fetch_http' isn't accurate based on the code flow shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — URL rewriting turns protocol-relative links such as //cdn.example.com/a into paths on the article host and leaves directory-relative links unresolved, breaking imported links and images.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 52-71, the code only handles URLs that start with '/'. For protocol-relative links like '//cdn.example.com/a', the condition `href.start_with?('/')` would be true, and it would incorrectly transform '//cdn.example.com/a' to 'http://eviltrout.com//cdn.example.com/a' (after the sub removes leading slashes, it becomes 'http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/a'). This is indeed a bug - protocol-relative URLs should be left alone or handled differently. The code doesn't check for '//' prefix before applying the transformation, so it will corrupt protocol-relative URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Replacing PostCreator with import_remote drops the original created_at value, so imported Disqus topics receive today's date while their replies retain historical dates.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the old code at line 144 was: `creator = PostCreator.new(user, title: t[:title], raw: "\[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})\]", created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)`. This passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` to preserve the original date. The new code at line 144 is: `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. Looking at TopicEmbed.import_remote, it calls TopicEmbed.import, which uses PostCreator.new without any created_at parameter. This means the original created_at from the Disqus thread is indeed lost, and imported topics will get the current date instead of their historical date. This is a real functional regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true` drops any pre-existing `topic_embeds` table before migration, permanently deleting its embedded-discussion mappings and posts' linkage data.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to `force: true` in the create_table statement for topic_embeds migration. Looking at the diff, this is a new table being created (the migration file is new: `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`). Since this is a brand new feature being added (topic embedding functionality), there is no pre-existing topic_embeds table to drop. The `force: true` option would only be problematic if this migration were run multiple times or if there was already a topic_embeds table, but in a normal migration scenario for a new feature, this table doesn't exist yet. Additionally, looking at the context, this appears to be part of a new embedding feature being introduced, so there's no existing data to lose. The finding is speculative about a scenario that wouldn't occur in normal usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Adding `force: true` to this existing migration drops a pre-existing `top_topics` table before recreation, permanently deleting cached topic-ranking data when the migration is rerun or unrecorded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb, the migration was changed from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. Adding `force: true` means that if the table already exists, it will be dropped before being recreated. This is a real problem because: 1) If this migration has already been run in production and the table exists with data, re-running migrations (which shouldn't normally happen but can in certain scenarios) would delete all data in that table. 2) More importantly, if there's already a top_topics table from a previous migration or manual creation, this migration will silently drop it and lose data. This is a legitimate concern for data integrity in database migrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — import` mutates the caller-owned `contents` string, so reusing it appends duplicate footers and creates spurious revisions.

adjudication.rationale:
Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, the code does `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "`. The `<<` operator mutates the original string in place. If the caller passes a string and later reuses it (e.g., in a loop), the footer would be appended multiple times. Looking at the callers in the diff: `poll_feed.rb` calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` inside a loop with `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` - each iteration creates a new string, so no issue there. `import_remote` creates a new `doc.content` each time. However, the finding is technically correct that the method mutates its input parameter, which is a code smell and could cause issues if the caller reuses the string. The test in topic_embed_spec.rb shows `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, title, contents)` being called twice with the same `contents` variable, which would result in duplicate footers. This is a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key` is never consumed by the polling path, leaving dead cache-key code that misleads maintainers into expecting conditional feed fetching.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, I can see the `feed_key` method is defined on lines 20-22 but is never called anywhere in the `poll_feed` method or `execute` method. The method creates a cache key but it's not used for any conditional fetching or caching logic. This is indeed dead code - the method exists but serves no purpose in the current implementation. However, this is more of a code quality/dead code issue rather than a bug that causes incorrect behavior. The code still functions correctly, it just has an unused method. This is borderline - it's technically a real issue (dead code) but it's more of a code smell than a defect that affects correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — The unbounded, timeout-free remote read runs in a Sidekiq job, so a slow or never-ending embedded page can occupy workers and leave discussions stuck loading.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb:48, the code uses `open(url).read` without any timeout configuration. This is called from `import_remote` which is invoked from `TopicRetriever.fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:51) and from `Jobs::PollFeed.poll_feed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:27). The TopicRetriever is called from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:15). These are indeed Sidekiq jobs. The `open(url).read` from the 'open-uri' library by default has no timeout, meaning a slow or hanging remote server could block the worker indefinitely. This is a real operational concern - unbounded network operations in background jobs can exhaust worker pools.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — The feed is fetched without a timeout or response-size limit, so a stalled or oversized feed can tie up the scheduled worker and stop feed imports.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29, the code uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` from the 'open-uri' library without any timeout or size limit parameters. This is a real concern - if the feed URL points to a slow server or returns an extremely large response, the scheduled worker could hang indefinitely or consume excessive memory. The open-uri library does support timeout options like `open_timeout` and `read_timeout` that are not being used here. This is a legitimate operational/reliability issue in the new code being added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — Disabling retries drops transient fetch, parse, or database failures until the next hourly invocation, leaving imported discussions stale for up to an hour.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to `sidekiq_options retry: false` on line 12 of poll_feed.rb. This is a scheduled job that runs hourly (`recurrence { hourly }`). The finding claims that disabling retries means transient failures (network issues, parsing errors, database problems) will cause the job to fail silently and not retry until the next hourly invocation. This is technically accurate - if the RSS feed fetch fails due to a temporary network issue, the job won't retry and will wait until the next hour. However, this is a deliberate design choice for a scheduled polling job. Retrying a failed feed poll immediately could cause issues (hammering a temporarily unavailable server, etc.). The hourly schedule provides natural retry behavior. This is more of a design decision than a bug - many scheduled jobs intentionally disable retries because they'll run again on schedule anyway. The 'staleness' concern is subjective and depends on requirements not specified in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Separating SETNX from EXPIRE lets a crash or Redis error leave a permanent throttle key, after which that embed URL is silently skipped forever.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 25-30, the code uses SETNX followed by EXPIRE as separate operations. If the process crashes or Redis fails between SETNX and EXPIRE, the key would be set without an expiration, causing it to persist indefinitely. This would mean that specific embed_url would be permanently throttled and never retrieved again. This is a real race condition/reliability bug. The fix would be to use SET with EX/NX options in a single atomic operation, or use a Lua script.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — RSS item HTML reaches raw_html cooking without sanitization, allowing feed-provided scripts and event handlers to execute on the forum origin.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code flow: In topic_embed.rb, the import method creates posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. In post.rb, when cook_method is raw_html, the cook method returns raw directly without any sanitization: 'return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]'. The content comes from RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb uses CGI.unescapeHTML on content) or from ruby-readability parsing. While readability does filter to specific tags, the RSS feed path in poll_feed.rb line 33-34 takes i.content directly and passes it to TopicEmbed.import. The content is then stored and rendered as raw HTML. This means any malicious HTML in the RSS feed (scripts, event handlers on allowed tags) would be rendered without sanitization on the forum's origin, creating an XSS vulnerability.
